set.outcome:
**AI 2 is an inbox, and your words become cards in it while you talk.** [Open it](/framework/ai2/). A box you talk to at the top; under it every card there is, newest first and unread first of all. Say something and it is a card on screen in 43 milliseconds, in your own words. About three seconds later that same card renames itself into what the fast assistant made of it — a title, a short reading, the names it minted, your own sentences folded underneath. One card the whole time: no duplicate, no flicker, no jump.

Every card carries **one flag** and nothing else — press it, type a line, and that sentence reaches you-know-who and redirects the work. Select text inside a card first and the same flag carries that exact quote. There is no Approve anywhere; opening a card is the only thing that marks it read. Mastermind notes render as notes, and the day's landed work is a card in the same stream, so "what I said" and "what happened" are one list.

![The AI 2 inbox at 1280](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/inbox-model/shots/inbox-1280.png)

**Proven by driving it, 11 checks of 11, on the worktree and again on the main tree.** 312 cards on screen; 312 = board ids ∪ prompt ids ∪ landed tasks, compared as sets from one snapshot so a mismatch would name the id. A real sentence posted to the log became a card in 43ms and a named card 2.5s later, one row, no duplicate. Read, flag, and span-flag each wrote their line and the flag showed up in the mastermind's inbox. With the assistant pointed at a dead port the page still drew 289 cards from the two static files and said it was off. Zero console errors, zero failed requests, at 400 and at 1280.

**Two invisible bugs found and fixed on the way.** The flag over a selected span was placed 38px above the selection with no clamp, so selecting near the top of the screen put it off-screen — nothing threw, the gesture just did nothing. And a prompt written before the log had ids was named by its position in a rolling window, so that name meant a different sentence once an old line fell off the end — which would have moved your flag from one sentence onto another. Both are written down beside the code.

**Deliberately left:** no filter row (300 unread is what the inbox honestly holds on day one; which filter you actually want is worth learning from using it, and guessing would put back the chrome this page exists to remove). The `ai2-` class prefix is not in `styles/css-scopes.txt` — that file is outside this task's fence, so one line is left for whoever holds it next; nothing collides today. The code came to 515 lines rather than the brief's 400, all of it working; cutting further would have meant cutting the comments.
